questions.question: What does the Claude Agent SDK give you that a loop library like Pydantic AI doesn't?
options: A full harness: Claude Code's loop, built-in file and shell tools, sessions and permission system
questions.explanation: The SDK runs Claude Code and streams its messages. You configure policy instead of writing the loop and tools.

questions.question: Bash is in allowed_tools, and a PreToolUse hook denies 'rm -rf'. The model calls Bash('rm -rf build'). What happens?
options: It runs, because Bash is allowed
The hook denies it; hooks are checked before allow rules
questions.explanation: Hooks run first, so a pattern-specific deny beats a tool-wide allow.

questions.question: You add a custom tool word_count to an SDK MCP server named 'docs'. What name goes in allowed_tools?
questions.explanation: MCP tools are exposed as mcp__<server>__<tool>, and allow rules use that full name.

questions.question: When is the can_use_tool callback asked?
options: Only when no hook, rule or permission mode already decided
questions.explanation: It's the last layer. Rules and modes that decide first mean your callback is never consulted for those calls.

questions.question: A denied tool call in this lesson comes back to the model as what?
options: An exception that ends the run
A tool_result with is_error true and the denial reason, so the model can adapt and explain
Nothing; the call is silently skipped
questions.explanation: Denials are observations. The model saw 'blocked' and told the user it didn't delete build/.

questions.question: When is permission_mode='bypassPermissions' reasonable?
options: On a developer laptop with real credentials
Inside an isolated container or VM with nothing valuable to lose
questions.explanation: Bypass removes the safety layers. Only use it where the sandbox itself is the safety boundary.
